purpose: Canonical contract for derived product/journey/capability/use-case/source/data/evolution graphs consumed by AI, developers, generated guides and Admin Development Intelligence.

views.orientation: Product -> audience -> journey -> capability -> implementation state -> roadmap. Default for a new developer/product owner.
views.business: Journey/capability/use-case graph with implementation details hidden.
views.developer: Journey/use case -> route -> implementation -> domain/data owner -> verification graph.
views.ai: Semantic ID/source-authority graph first, then developer/deep graph; filenames are evidence, not inferred ownership.
views.deep: Class/interface/inheritance/dependency graph for debugging and low-level analysis.

mapping_rules: Authored journey/use-case/domain/schema/stage authorities supply semantic nodes before source scanning.
Source scanning may enrich implementation/dependency edges but must not invent product ownership.
Missing mappings remain explicit gap nodes; they must not be silently inferred from similarly named files/classes/functions.
Every derived semantic record retains its source authority path or source-code path.
Generated audience guides are projections of the same graph and may hide implementation details, never redefine semantics.

snapshot_policy.canonical_key: accepted Git SHA when available; otherwise exact candidate SHA for non-release analysis
snapshot_policy.request_rule: Never scan source or rebuild graph in an HTTP request.
snapshot_policy.invalidation: A source/contract/package change marks affected semantic owners stale without forcing immediate rebuild.
snapshot_policy.single_flight: Only one rebuild per graph scope/SHA may execute concurrently.
snapshot_policy.history: Keep accepted-SHA snapshots and precomputed adjacent diffs for architecture time travel.

storage.current_pointer: cache/redis may point to latest completed snapshot; it is not authority

admin_policy.default_behavior: Serve latest completed semantic snapshot immediately; show staleness, mapping gaps and offer refresh when needed.
admin_policy.polling: Do not poll when idle. If a rebuild is active, use sparse status refresh or a lightweight event.
